newsitem.title: UK: Hunting Cargo Air moves to Irish register.
newsitem.headline: Hunting Cargo Air moves to Irish register.

text.p: UK carrier Hunting Cargo Airlines said it was in the process of transferring the three remaining aircraft it has on the UK register to the Irish register.

Commercial manager Steve Guynan told Reuters that once the certification transfer of three Lockheed Electras was completed by the end of this month, the carrier, part of Hunting Plc, will be known as Hunting Cargo Airlines (Ireland).
The remainder of the airline's owned fleet comprises three Electras and six Boeing 727 freighters, all of which are registered in Ireland.
"We are making the transfer because Ireland's aircraft operating regulations are the same as those practised in the rest of Europe -- with the exception of the UK," he said.

"The UK Civil Aviation Authority adopts a different stance to the rest of Europe in certain areas. For example, even though the 727 has been operating as a freighter for a number of years, in Britain it is regarded as a new aircraft type," he said.

Guynen added that when Hunting Cargo applied to register its 727Fs with the CAA, the authority said it wanted to undertake a detailed investigation of the aircraft type but could not estimate a time scale or give a costing.

"We are a business and we had to take a business decision by registering all of our aircraft in Ireland. We are not trying to pan the CAA but it is of no use to us to have duplicated registrations and overheads," he said.
Hunting Cargo, which lists DHL Worldwide Express amongs its leasing customers, also flies four 727Fs for their owner, TNT Express Worldwide, and leases one Lockheed Hercules.

Guynan said earlier on Wednesday that the airline was bidding to win a contract to fly up to five converted Airbus A300B4 freighters on behalf of DHL, which would probably lease these planes. -Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
